authored_excerpt: Replying to a reader who connected his media criticism with political analysis, Rosen explains that his media studies doctorate and journalism work could coexist in NYU's Arts and Sciences program.
A reader compares Rosen's approach to election stakes with George Lakoff's moral framing. Rosen replies that he has not met Lakoff but sees similarities in their approaches.
Responding to criticism that the Bangor Daily News values statement is too vague, Rosen says it makes progress in some areas while remaining limited in others.
In the discussion of the Bangor Daily News values statement, Rosen explains its limits as a desire to remain within the industry's consensus.
After a reader recommends KCRW's interview with Barton Gellman, Rosen praises The Journalist and the Firefighter and its follow-up as a rethinking of journalism he had hoped to hear.
Continuing his post about news subscription imagery, Rosen distinguishes reporting that makes readers feel present from a paid promise of knowledge withheld from others.

Asked whether insider journalism began with Evans and Novak, Rosen describes a longer commercialization process. He argues that media companies' control of distribution changed when the internet offered different terms.
Replying to Alex's suggested list of commentators in the discussion of newsroom bias, Rosen uses irony to show how an assertion of impartiality does not settle the underlying judgment.
Quoting his earlier post about platform audiences, Rosen corrects the attribution from the misspelled name in that post to Josh Marshall.
Quoting On the Media's question about why journalists took so long to reconsider their norms, Rosen points to his January 2017 PressThink essay Send the interns.
In a discussion about journalism's deterioration before Trump, Rosen links to a December 2006 PressThink post as an earlier example moving in the same direction.

Replying in a discussion of television stations' obligations around Trump-related advertising, Rosen offers a November 2004 PressThink post while acknowledging that it does not answer the precise question.
Following his revised recommendation of Lilliana Mason's work, Rosen explains that he had accidentally published a different draft the previous day.
In the discussion of Polarization Is Not the Problem, Rosen links to a 2024 Bluesky post that presents part of his earlier formulation.
Responding to a comment about earlier work by Ornstein and Mann, Rosen rejects the suggestion that the discussion claims these ideas had never been expressed before.
After James Brooks describes an Alaska Beacon decision guided by a citizens agenda, Rosen asks where the site presents the agenda itself rather than commentary about it.
Rosen connects his earlier thread about distinctions in media criticism with Brian Beutler's argument that exposure is not accountability.
